findings.title: credential-shaped literal (openai-style-key) in the manifest
findings.detail: Line 52 contains a value matching the openai-style-key pattern ('sk-tes***'). Treat it as compromised the moment it is pushed: it is in git history, in CI logs, and in every artifact rendered from this commit. A placeholder is not an exemption — placeholders get replaced with real values by the next person in a hurry, and the shape of the manifest is what teaches them where to put it.
findings.evidence: Evidence D: 'security scanner flagged a hard-coded API key pattern in the manifest'
findings.remediation: Remove the literal, reference a Secret via valueFrom.secretKeyRef, and rotate the credential if it was ever real.

findings.title: livenessProbe points at a dependency-aware path '/health' (identical to the readiness path)
findings.detail: Liveness answers 'is this process wedged'; readiness answers 'can this pod serve traffic right now'. Wiring liveness to a dependency-aware endpoint converts a downstream brownout into a fleet-wide restart storm: every pod fails liveness at once, every pod is killed, and the cold-start penalty is paid on all of them simultaneously while the dependency is still degraded.
findings.evidence: Evidence C: 'liveness should not depend on Redis or model backends'; Evidence D: 'one pod restarted after failing liveness during Redis brownout'
findings.remediation: Point livenessProbe at /live and leave readiness on the dependency-aware path.

findings.title: livenessProbe path '/health' is not the documented '/live'
findings.detail: The application contract documents only /live, /ready and /metrics. '/health' is undocumented: it may 404 (every pod fails its probe and the rollout stalls or crash-loops) or it may exist with different semantics than this probe needs.
findings.evidence: Evidence C: documented endpoints GET /live, GET /ready, GET /metrics

findings.title: readinessProbe path '/health' is not the documented '/ready'

findings.title: replicas (2) is below the documented safe floor (3)
findings.detail: Steady-state capacity would be 2 pods. The service is documented to need 3 healthy replicas, so a single node drain, eviction or crash takes the service below safe capacity with no rollout involved at all.
findings.evidence: Evidence C: 'minimum safe production capacity is 3 healthy replicas during rollout'

findings.title: resources.limits.cpu '500m' is below the floor '1' on container 'gateway'
findings.detail: Cutting limits.cpu from 1 to 500m shrinks per-pod headroom at the same time as the replica count drops. For a memory limit this is an OOMKill risk under load; for CPU it is throttling that shows up as tail latency, not as an error.
findings.evidence: Evidence D: p95 latency 180ms -> 950ms, 5xx rate 3.8% after a similar change in staging
findings.remediation: Keep resources.limits.cpu >= 1, or attach a load test and change the floor in solution/policy/guardrail.yaml deliberately.

findings.title: rollout can drop to 0 available pod(s); floor is 3
findings.detail: replicas=2, maxUnavailable=2, maxSurge=0. Worst case during the rollout is 2 - 2 = 0 available pods before any new pod becomes ready, and with maxSurge=0 no replacement pod can even be created until an old one is torn down. With a documented 20-40s warm-up, that window is minutes, not seconds.
findings.evidence: Evidence D: 'rollout took 6m and briefly ran with 2 available pods', p95 180ms -> 950ms, 5xx 3.8%
findings.remediation: Require spec.replicas - maxUnavailable >= 3. Prefer a surge-only rollout for this service: maxUnavailable: 0, maxSurge: 2.

findings.title: env OPENAI_API_KEY holds a literal value but must come from a secret
findings.detail: 'OPENAI_API_KEY' is classified as sensitive by policy. A literal value here is readable by anyone with repo access or pod-read access in the namespace.
findings.evidence: Evidence B: REDIS_URL moved from secretKeyRef to a literal; Evidence D: 'security scanner flagged a hard-coded API key pattern'
findings.remediation: Restore valueFrom.secretKeyRef for OPENAI_API_KEY. If the value genuinely changed, rotate it in the secret store and reference the new key.

findings.title: env REDIS_URL was a secretKeyRef and is now a plaintext value
findings.detail: The baseline sources this value from the 'inference-gateway-secrets' Secret. Inlining it moves the value into git history, into every rendered artifact, into CI logs and into `kubectl describe` output for anyone with pod-read access in the namespace. Rotation stops being a secret-store operation and becomes a code change, and the old value stays in git forever.
findings.evidence: Evidence B: REDIS_URL moved from secretKeyRef to a literal; Evidence D: 'security scanner flagged a hard-coded API key pattern'
findings.remediation: Restore valueFrom.secretKeyRef for REDIS_URL. If the value genuinely changed, rotate it in the secret store and reference the new key.

findings.title: liveness can kill container 'gateway' after ~30s, inside the documented 40s warm-up window
findings.detail: initialDelaySeconds=0 + periodSeconds=10 x failureThreshold=3 = 30s. A pod that takes the documented 40s to warm its routing tables is restarted before it ever becomes ready, producing a crash-loop that looks like an application bug. This is a pre-existing gap in the current manifest, not something this PR introduced.
findings.evidence: Evidence C: 'startup can take 20-40 seconds while model routing tables warm up'
findings.remediation: Add a startupProbe (e.g. periodSeconds: 5, failureThreshold: 18) so liveness only starts counting once the process is up.
